findings.summary: Engagement fees do not follow the work. The nine-month investor relations program and the eight-month crisis engagement cost the same $46,500 to $47,000 as the four-month media program and reputation audit, while a five-month executive messaging project costs $102,000.
findings.evidence: d:0018: the IR program will 'run for approximately nine months, and our fixed professional fee for the scope described in this letter is $47,000' (E-2018-001, about $5,500 a month). d:0022, d:0024 and d:0029 show what that fee buys: perception interviews, a results script and rehearsal, an investor targeting shortlist with one-page fund profiles, a 'weekly status note', a weekly coverage summary and roughly monthly working sessions, staffed by a Partner, a Senior Associate and an Analyst under the Managing Partner. d:0038: crisis counsel at $46,500 over about eight months (E-2021-001, about $5,900 a month). Compare d:0045, media relations 'for approximately four months' at $46,000 (about $11,600 a month); d:0075, an audit at $45,500 over about four months; and d:0061, executive messaging over 'approximately five months' at $102,000 (about $21,600 a month) with a team of the same size. At the firm's own FY2018 revenue per head (about $251,000 a year from the finance ledger and roster, so roughly $21,000 a month), the IR fee covers about a quarter of one person's time for a program run by four or five.

findings.summary: The four comparable fees fall by exactly $500 per engagement from 2018 to 2024 while the firm's revenue grows by about 40 percent, so the fees read as a counting sequence rather than a rate card.
findings.evidence: Fixed fees in date order: $47,000 (d:0018, June 2018), $46,500 (d:0038, July 2021), $46,000 (d:0045, April 2022), $45,500 (d:0075, February 2024). Over the same span the financial summaries show revenue rising from 2,766,000 (FY2018, d:0026) to 3,917,000 (FY2023, d:0074), and revenue per head rises with it. A firm whose revenue per head is climbing is raising its prices, not cutting the price of comparable programs by $500 at a time.

findings.summary: The crisis letter sells open-ended, after-hours crisis counsel of no fixed length for a fixed fee paid in equal monthly installments. A crisis firm would not sign those terms, and they cannot be invoiced as written.
findings.evidence: d:0038: services are 'adjusted as the Matter develops and as you direct'; 'During the acute phase we will be available outside ordinary business hours'; 'Should the Company need urgent support before that date, we will provide it and treat it as falling within this letter'; 'a fixed professional fee of $46,500, which covers the scope described above for the full term'; 'We will invoice the fixed fee in equal monthly installments over the term of the engagement', yet 'This engagement will continue until the services described above are complete', so there is no term to divide by. d:0039 adds a call with the client 'each weekday until the approval route is settled'. Crisis work is normally billed by the hour, or as a retainer with hourly overage, because its volume cannot be known at signing.

findings.summary: Travel snaps back past its pre-pandemic level in 2021. The FY2021 summary shows the firm's highest travel spend to that point, 22 percent above 2019, in a year whose client sessions in the sample were held by video.
findings.evidence: Travel: 196,520 in FY2019 (d:0031), 46,180 in FY2020 (d:0035), 239,370 in FY2021 (d:0043). The October 2021 working session d:0041 is 'Held by video conference', and so is the January 2022 one, d:0044. The recipe gives 2020's collapse as 'conferences and roadshows stopped'; in 2021 they had not come back above 2019 levels. The declared shock covers 2020 alone, so the ledger returns straight to its trend the following year.

findings.summary: Office & Facilities is identical to the dollar across consecutive years, three years at one figure and then four at the next. That reads as a budget plug, not an actual occupancy cost.
findings.evidence: Office & Facilities is 246,400 in FY2016, FY2017 and FY2018 (d:0001, d:0017, d:0026); 262,500 in FY2019, FY2020, FY2021 and FY2022 (d:0031, d:0035, d:0043, d:0058); and 291,600 in FY2023 (d:0074). Every other expense line moves every year. A line that carries utilities, supplies and maintenance as well as rent does not repeat exactly, and even a flat-rent lease would not produce seven years of two exact values.

findings.summary: No defect claimed: the overall P&L fits an 11- to 15-person communications and IR boutique, and the declared 2020 reads correctly. The defects above sit in the fee schedule and in individual expense lines, not in the firm's scale.
findings.evidence: From the finance ledger and the roster: revenue per head of roughly $215,000 to $285,000, compensation at 49 to 60 percent of revenue, and net margin of 16 to 24 percent, which is plausible for a partner-owned LLC. FY2020 (d:0035) is flat on FY2019 with a soft second quarter (610,642 against 870,116 in Q1) and travel cut to 46,180.
